title: Whole-of-Government Response to the 2019 Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV)
what_it_is: Whole-of-Government Response to the 2019 Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV)

sections.label: Multi-Ministry Taskforce and WHO alert
sections.summary: Singapore set up a Multi-Ministry Taskforce before its first confirmed imported case, and WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 30 January.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Singapore Government has set up a Multi-Ministry Taskforce to coordinate the whole-of-Government efforts to combat this outbreak even before the first confirmed imported case occurred here.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: On 30 January, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that the outbreak constituted a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, raising the global alert levels.

sections.label: Assistance package for China
sections.summary: Singapore will put together an assistance package to help communities in China severely affected by the novel coronavirus.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For this reason, Singapore will be putting together an assistance package to help the communities in China severely affected by the novel coronavirus.

sections.label: Taskforce set up 22 January
sections.summary: By 22 January 2020, over 500 confirmed cases and 17 deaths were reported in China when the Multi-Ministry Taskforce was decided to be set up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: By 22 January 2020, over 500 confirmed cases were reported in China with a death toll of 17, when we decided to set up the Multi-Ministry Taskforce.

sections.label: Latest WHO case figures
sections.summary: The latest WHO report showed more than 14,000 reported cases in China and 304 deaths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The latest WHO report showed that there were more than 14,000 reported cases in China and 304 deaths.

sections.label: Infectiousness and limited asymptomatic spread
sections.summary: For coronaviruses generally, a person is most infectious when symptomatic, likely also for the novel coronavirus, with evidence of limited spread from a person without symptoms during incubation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For coronaviruses generally, the person is most infectious when he is displaying symptoms or what you call symptomatic, and this is likely to be the case for the novel coronavirus as well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: There is evidence of limited spread from a person without symptoms during the incubation period.

sections.label: Symptoms, treatment and fatality rate
sections.summary: Exposed persons may be well for a few days before symptoms like fever or cough; there is no known curative treatment, and the case fatality rate is about 2% to 3%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Persons exposed to the virus may be well for a few days before developing symptoms, such as fever or cough.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: There is currently no known curative treatment for the novel coronavirus.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Development of a successful cure may take time, maybe months or years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The current case fatality rate stands at about 2% to 3%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The fatality rate seems lower than SARS, which was around 10%.

sections.label: Taskforce stepped up measures
sections.summary: The Taskforce has stepped up measures as the global and local situation evolves, considering factors including impact on society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As the global and local situation evolves, the Taskforce has stepped up our measures accordingly, taking into careful consideration relevant factors, including the impact on our society.

sections.label: Confirmed cases and community spread
sections.summary: All confirmed cases are Wuhan residents or recent travellers to Wuhan, with no evidence of community spread in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: All of our confirmed cases are Wuhan residents or persons who had recently travelled to Wuhan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: There is no evidence of community spread in Singapore.

sections.label: Quarantine and active surveillance
sections.summary: Close contacts are quarantined 14 days from last contact; other contacts undergo active surveillance with daily MOH health checks due to lower risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For close contacts, they will be put under quarantine for 14 days since their last contact with the confirmed case.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For other contacts, they will be put on active surveillance with daily health checks by MOH, as the risk of infection is lower for them.

sections.label: SARS outbreak duration
sections.summary: SARS took about eight months from the first detected case in November 2002 until WHO declared the outbreak contained in July 2003.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: SARS took about eight months from the first detected case in November 2002 till the WHO declared the SARS outbreak contained in July 2003.

sections.label: Community spread in other places
sections.summary: There could be community spread in more Chinese cities beyond Wuhan or in other countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: First, there could be community spread in more Chinese cities beyond Wuhan or in other countries.

sections.label: Measures for extensive community spread
sections.summary: If community spread becomes very extensive, measures to reduce human-to-human interactions will be considered, and the virus could mutate into a pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: If the community spread becomes very extensive, we will need to consider measures to reduce human-to-human interactions, such as cancelling mass gatherings, suspending schools, paring down non-essential care services and introducing further infection control and monitoring measures, to slow the spread.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Third, the virus could mutate to become more infectious and spread widely, resulting in a pandemic.

sections.label: Isolation bed capacity increase
sections.summary: Isolation bed capacity was increased by around 100 in the past two weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, we have increased our capacity of isolation beds by around 100 in the past two weeks.

sections.label: PRC travellers to Singapore
sections.summary: About 14,000 PRC travellers flew to Singapore daily, falling over 80% after China's 23 January outbound restrictions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Typically, there will be about 14,000 People's Republic of China (PRC) travellers flying in from China to Singapore every day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: After the Chinese imposed outbound restrictions on 23 January, this number came down sharply by more than 80%, just through the Chinese measures alone.

sections.label: Travel history visitor restrictions
sections.summary: On 28 January new visitors with recent Hubei travel history were disallowed, and on 31 January those with travel history in the rest of mainland China.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Early last week, when we saw the sharply accelerating trend of infection among the population of Chinese nationals from Hubei province, we knew we had to move.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that is why on 28 January, we decided to disallow all new visitors with recent travel history in Hubei.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: While the majority of confirmed cases in China were still linked to Hubei province, it was evident that the virus had spread to every region of mainland China and there was a high risk of widespread community transmission in other parts of China.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And so, on 31 January, last Friday, we decided to take the additional precaution of disallowing all new visitors with recent travel history in the rest of mainland China.

sections.label: Confirmed and suspect cases
sections.summary: As of 8.00 am there were 18 confirmed cases, 240 suspect cases testing negative, and 43 suspect cases pending results.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As of 8.00 am today, we have 18 confirmed cases of the virus, all with recent travel history in Hubei, as Minister Gan Kim Yong mentioned earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Sixteen are PRC nationals, mostly here on short-term passes and the other two are Singaporeans who were among the 92 who came back recently from Wuhan after the city was locked down.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Beyond the confirmed cases, we have tested a broader group of 240 suspect cases, all of whom are negative; and then there are another 43 suspect cases, for which test results are pending.

sections.label: Persons under quarantine
sections.summary: As of last night, 524 persons were under quarantine, 222 in Government Quarantine Facilities and 302 at home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As of last night, there are 524 persons under quarantine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Two hundred and twenty-two are in Government Quarantine Facilities (GQF), and 302 are serving quarantine at home.

sections.label: Leave of Absence for returning residents
sections.summary: Returning residents and long-term pass holders assessed as lower risk are asked to take a 14-day Leave of Absence from their return date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our assessment is that they are of lower risk compared to those who were recently in Hubei.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, for all such returning residents and long-term pass holders, we ask them to take a 14-day Leave of Absence (LOA) from the date of their return.

sections.label: Masks released to retailers
sections.summary: In the nine days before 29 January, the Government released over five million masks from its stockpile to retailers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the nine days leading up to end of 29 January, the Government released more than five million masks from our stockpile to the retailers.

sections.label: Change in mask distribution method
sections.summary: Due to rapid consumption and potential threat to supply lines, the method of distributing masks from the national stockpile was changed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Because of the rapid consumption rate that we had seen earlier and the potential threat to our supply lines, we decided to change the method of distribution of masks from our national stockpile.

sections.label: Mask collection figures
sections.summary: Mask collection began on Saturday 1 February, and over 200,000 packs, or 15% of the total, have been collected to date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The collection of masks started on 1 February, on Saturday, and, to date, more than 200,000 packs, or 15% of the total, have been collected.

sections.label: Support package for companies and workers
sections.summary: A package of measures to help viable companies stay afloat and workers stay in jobs will be announced during the Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Besides these specific sectors, we recognise that there will be knock-on impacts on related industries in the event of a broad-based slowdown.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we are working out a package of measures to help viable companies stay afloat and to help workers stay in their jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This package of measures will be announced during the Budget.

sections.label: Hoarding, profiteering and falsehoods
sections.summary: There are examples of people hoarding and profiteering from mask sales and spreading falsehoods online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, there are other examples, too – people hoarding and profiteering from the sale of masks; people spreading falsehoods online.

sections.label: Anti-PRC sentiment and discrimination
sections.summary: Anti-PRC sentiment has emerged, with reports of discrimination against PRC nationals by landlords and service providers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Anti-PRC sentiment has also emerged amongst some groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: On the ground, you hear reports of discrimination against PRC nationals, whether it is landlords denying them their tenancy or service providers denying them service.

sections.label: Singaporeans helping during Wuhan outbreak
sections.summary: NUS students organise a 24-hour e-gaming tournament for students on LOA, and Scoot pilots, crew and MFA officials volunteered despite risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At NUS, I understand that students are even organising a 24-hour e-gaming tournament to keep the students on LOA occupied.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We see shining examples of selfless acts by Singaporeans in the Scoot pilots and crew of TR121 who volunteered to fly the 92 Singaporeans from Wuhan despite the risks to themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Two Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) officials volunteered for this assignment despite the risks and are being quarantined when they came back.

sections.label: Singaporeans in Wuhan and Beijing Mission
sections.summary: About 90-plus Singaporeans were in the last exercise, four could not return, and about 140 remain in Wuhan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Our Beijing Mission is in touch with them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, in the last exercise, there were about 90-plus Singaporeans and four of them were unable to come back because they had already shown symptoms: one was hospitalised and three of them had shown symptoms and they were deemed not fit to fly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The vast majority of this group had come back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We believe that there are still about 140 Singaporeans in Wuhan now.

sections.label: Singaporeans outside Hubei infected
sections.summary: No Singaporeans outside of Hubei are known to be infected with the virus at this point in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On whether there are any Singaporeans outside of Hubei who have been infected with the virus, we do not know of anyone at this point in time.

sections.label: Economic impact and Budget measures
sections.summary: There will be an overall economic impact, so measures and a strong Budget package are being studied, with interim initiatives rolled out quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, there will be an overall impact on the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why I said we are studying this very carefully to develop a series of measures and a strong package in the Budget to help companies and workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the interim, wherever we can, we will develop and quickly roll out initiatives to help firms without having to wait for the Budget.

sections.label: No coronavirus-free certification
sections.summary: There is no such thing as a coronavirus-free certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Actually, there is no such thing as a coronavirus-free certification.

sections.label: No virus-free certificate possible
sections.summary: A person may be virus-free at that moment but within the incubation period, so no hospital or screening centre can certify he is virus-free.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: He may be virus-free at that moment, but he may already have been infected but is within the incubation period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, it is not possible for our hospital or for any screening centre to give a certificate that this person is virus-free.

sections.label: No virus-free certificates
sections.summary: It is not possible to give a free-from-disease certificate, and employers are urged not to send workers to hospitals for virus-free testing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, it is not possible to give a free-from-disease certificate, as what Dr Lily Neo was alluding to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I would also like to take this opportunity to urge employers not to send their workers to our hospitals for testing in order to certify their workers as virus-free.

sections.label: Certificates load hospitals unnecessarily
sections.summary: Such certificates cannot be issued and would load hospitals unnecessarily, while ambulance services have been ramped up for the outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: It is just not possible for such certificates to be issued and you will just load the hospital unnecessarily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We have ramped up our ambulance services in order to respond to this outbreak situation.

sections.label: Enough healthcare workers for cases
sections.summary: The question asks whether there are enough healthcare workers and professionals to manage patient cases in NCID and hospitals amid increased demand and work stresses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Do we have enough healthcare workers and professionals to help manage patient cases in NCID and the hospitals in this period of heightened healthcare alert seeing to the increased demand and work stresses on them?

sections.label: Sustainable long-term duty planning
sections.summary: Group chief executive officers were reminded to plan long term, with sustainable duty schedules and rosters ensuring sufficient turnaround and rest for doctors and healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I reminded the group chief executive officers just recently that we need to plan for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: It is not dash to the end point because we need to be prepared that this may take months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, whatever duty schedules, rosters and so on have to be planned on a sustainable basis to ensure there is sufficient turnaround and sufficient rest given to our doctors, healthcare workers so that they are able to sustain in the long term.

sections.label: Postponing non-urgent medical care
sections.summary: Some non-urgent medical care, such as some elective procedures, may need to be postponed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Some of the medical care that is non-urgent, some of the elective procedures, for example, may need to be postponed.

sections.label: Overseas trips to China postponed
sections.summary: All overseas trips to China from primary schools to tertiary have been postponed, and the Taskforce met daily and made three major decisions last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for overseas trips, all overseas trips to China have now been postponed, from primary schools all the way to tertiary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Last week alone, we made three major decisions because the Taskforce met every day to monitor the situation.

sections.label: Quarantine for recent China travellers
sections.summary: People possibly exposed, including recent returnees from China and Hubei, are quarantined to be safe, but quarantine does not mean infection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Yes, they have been subject to some exposure perhaps through close contacts, perhaps they have been back home from China recently, particularly in Hubei, so we want them to be quarantined just to be safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we should not assume automatically that anyone in quarantine is infected.

sections.label: Cleaning confirmed case sites
sections.summary: Confirmed cases trigger thorough cleaning and disinfection supervised by NEA, and Singapore must prepare for more cases and community spread.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I do not know if I have touched objects or places around me or contaminated, and if I touched them, I might get sick.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, thirdly, whenever there is a confirmed case, there is a thorough cleaning and disinfection process to make sure the place is entirely cleaned and disinfected, and NEA supervises that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In fact, this is critical because if the situation were to escalate, as Minister Gan Kim Yong said, we have to be prepared for things to get worse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have to be prepared for more cases in Singapore even for community spread.

sections.label: Self-employed lose income on LOA
sections.summary: Employers pay employees on leave of absence, but self-employed persons at home for 14 days lose their income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For employees who have LOAs in which employers pay for them when they are on leave, but for the self-employed, there is this element whereby if I am at home for 14 days, I do not have the income.

sections.label: Support for quarantine allowance seekers
sections.summary: There is a quarantine allowance, and help is being sought while immediate support measures are studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There is quarantine allowance and they are seeking some help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are studying if there are some immediate measures that can be put in place to support and help them.

sections.label: Isolated patients improving in hospitals
sections.summary: All patients are isolated and supported in hospitals, most are improving, and discharge is hoped for soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: All of them are isolated and being supported in our hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Most of them are improving and we hope to be able to see a discharge soon.

sections.label: Action against irresponsible landlords
sections.summary: If a landlord irresponsibly evicts a tenant without basis, possible actions against the landlord will be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For specific cases, let us say it is a landlord that is taking a very irresponsible action to evict a tenant without any basis, then we will see if some actions can be taken against the landlord because, again, doing something like this is not just an individual action.

sections.label: China restricting its people's travel
sections.summary: China has restricted its own people from travelling outside China because it does not want to spread the virus to other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: China itself has restricted its own people from travelling outside of China precisely because they do not want to spread this virus to other countries.

sections.label: Singapore's role in global solutions
sections.summary: Singapore is part of finding solutions to the global emergency through vaccines, medical discoveries and best practices, with collaborative research efforts on treatment and vaccines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Essentially, how is Singapore also being part of the solution to find solutions to the global emergency in terms of vaccines, medical discoveries and best practices to contain the virus so that Singaporeans benefit, the region and the wider global community of nations benefit?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: There are collaborative efforts between our research institutions to look for a solution both in terms of treatment as well as vaccines.

sections.label: China sequencing virus on WHO website
sections.summary: China sequenced the virus early and posted it on the WHO website so research institutions globally could access it and carry out their own research.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: China, for example, has, very early on, already sequenced the virus and it was posted on the WHO website so that all the research institutions globally can have access to the sequencing, so that they are able to carry out their own research and enhance the knowledge and understanding of the virus.

sections.label: Widespread community transmission scenario
sections.summary: Widespread community transmission means multiple clusters with no clear links to any source, direct person-to-person transmission and no way to contact trace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And therefore, the likelihood of a widespread community transmission is less likely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But there is also a scenario which I mentioned in my speech, where there is widespread community transmission, meaning there will be multiple clusters of infection where there are no clear links to any source of infection.Therefore, you would then assess that it may be transmitting from one person to another quite directly and there is no way for us to have contact tracing for them because they have many, many contacts.

sections.label: Cancelling gatherings and suspending schools
sections.summary: Measures include cancelling major gatherings of thousands of people and possibly suspending some or all schools to minimise interaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: One example is to cancel or terminate all the major gatherings where you have thousands and thousands of people, as well as to minimise the risks of transmission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: There is also the possibility that we may suspend some schools or all schools, depending on the situation so as to minimise the interaction of children at schools as well as the parent interaction.

sections.label: Using PCA for price controls
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government will consider deploying the PCA to put price controls in place for limited periods in crisis situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: You can create "black markets" and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But for exceptional and crisis situations like this, is deploying the PCA to actually put price controls in place, using this legislation, something that the Government will consider, in future, just for limited periods of time?

sections.label: Letters of demand to e-commerce platforms
sections.summary: Letters of demand were sent to Lazada and Carousell to request information on potential profiteers on their platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Letters of demand (LODs) have also been sent to other e-commerce platforms like Lazada and Carousell to request information on any potential profiteers on their platform.

sections.label: Mask distribution via collection exercise
sections.summary: Postal mask distribution risked wastage, so a decentralised collection exercise at void decks and RC centres was used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the second supplementary question, we had deliberated over this and we felt that if you were to distribute masks via post, there may well be wastage because some households will not need the masks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: You save it, either for your stockpile or you give it to someone else." So, in that sense, a collection exercise would be a more prudent way of distributing masks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And to address the concern of people gathering together, we had decentralised the distribution points to void decks, RC centres.

sections.label: N95 masks in community transmission
sections.summary: Wearing N95 masks is probably not the solution in the event of widespread community transmission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Maybe I should explain that in the event of widespread community transmission, wearing N95 masks is probably not the solution.

sections.label: Social distancing instead of N95 masks
sections.summary: Social distancing, managing crowd gathering and minimising human-to-human interaction are likely to be introduced rather than N95 masks for general use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In fact, we are most likely going to introduce social distancing, as I mentioned, manage the crowd gathering, minimising human-to-human interaction, rather than to introduce the N95 mask for general use.

sections.label: Protection for frontline healthcare workers
sections.summary: Healthcare workers are a most important resource in an outbreak and need adequate protection as they face the disease and patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Healthcare workers are one of our most important resources in a disease outbreak like this, and they are right at the frontline, they are facing the disease and the patients every day, every hour, and, therefore, we need to make sure that they have adequate protection.

sections.label: PPE protocols at NCID
sections.summary: NCID has protocols for putting on and taking off PPE, with a second person monitoring, and exposure requires quarantine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In NCID, for example, there are well-established protocols, including monitoring of how you put on your Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) or how you take it off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: There is also a second person monitoring how you do it to make sure that you follow every step carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Once you miss a step and are exposed, you will have to be quarantined to make sure that you are not infected.

sections.label: Patient triage at clinics
sections.summary: Patients will be triaged as soon as they arrive at their clinic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As soon as patients arrive at their clinic, they will be triaged.

sections.label: Minister on task force
sections.summary: The Minister for Communications and Information is part of the task force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In fact, the Minister for Communications and Information is part of the task force.

sections.label: NEA cleaning confirmed case premises
sections.summary: For confirmed cases, NEA officers supervise and nominated trained contractors clean and disinfect premises to prevent further spread.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Especially for the confirmed case, NEA officers will be on the ground to provide supervision and they will also have nominated contractors that are trained to follow a certain protocol to clean and disinfect the premises to prevent further spread of the disease.

sections.label: Employer advisory on LOA support
sections.summary: An advisory was sent to employers on supporting the LOA requirement, with suggestions such as additional, paid vacation or sick leave.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is an important area to look into.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We have sent out an advisory to employers that because this LOA is a requirement, they will have to find ways of supporting it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Whether the person who is on LOA is provided with additional leave or that the duration of LOA is treated as paid vacation leave or sick leave, there are certain suggestions on how the employers may treat it.

sections.label: Support for self-employed persons
sections.summary: The government is mindful of the impact on self-employed persons and is looking at ways to be helpful.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Member has also asked the question about self-employed persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We are very mindful of how they could be impacted and, as Minister Lawrence Wong has said earlier, we are looking at ways in which we can be helpful.

sections.label: Discharge testing and doctor assessment
sections.summary: Patients do two tests one day apart that must be negative, and doctors assess them before discharge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: First, the way I understand from my professional colleagues, that for patients, they will do two tests and both tests have to show negative, and they are usually one day apart to make sure that they are free of virus before they are considered for discharge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But on top of that, at the end, doctors usually will make an assessment at the end of the day despite all the tests that we do, to assess and be confident that the person is well, does not look sick, does not have symptoms and generally are quite well, and maybe he will keep him for a while longer to make sure that there is no further deterioration before his discharge.

sections.label: No reports of incidence
sections.summary: No report of such an incidence has been received so far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are all looking out for such an incidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So far, we have not received any report of such an incidence.

sections.label: 30,000 work pass holders returning
sections.summary: News of 30,000 work pass holders returning caused anxiety as most live in HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the news on 30,000 work pass holders returning to Singapore has caused some anxiety to our residents because as the main bulk of this 30,000 work pass holders are living in our HDB flats.

sections.label: Travel restrictions from Hong Kong
sections.summary: Travel restrictions in place apply to Mainland China, not Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The third question, will we impose or is there any plan to impose travel restrictions for those who come from Hong Kong?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The travel restrictions that we have put in place apply to Mainland China.

sections.label: 30,000 Work Permit holders in China
sections.summary: The 30,000 Work Permit holders are still in China and not all live in housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the 30,000 Work Permit holders, I should clarify they are still in China now, they have not come back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Not all of them live in our housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we are doing a tabulation, working directly with the employers to identify who they are, which sectors, where are their places of residence today.

sections.label: Virus response and organ failure
sections.summary: When the body cannot eliminate the virus, organs may fail and death can occur.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Basically, when the virus attacks your body, your body will try to mount a response, a defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And very often, you find that when your body is unable to respond adequately to eliminate the virus, your body will go into a shock, your organs go into overdrive and, therefore, you may begin to see organ failures and, eventually, death will occur as a result.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, because of this, chances are, if you already have underlying medical conditions, your body is already weak, your defences are weak and your organs may already be impaired, therefore, the risk of death is higher.

sections.label: Less fatal than SARS
sections.summary: Numerically and statistically, it is less fatal than SARS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, can we have some verification whether this is true so far?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, numerically, statistically, it is less fatal than SARS.

sections.label: Fatality rates SARS and coronavirus
sections.summary: The passage states both numbers change over time and that as of today the coronavirus appears less fatal, with SARS at 10% and coronavirus at 2% to 3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, therefore, both number will change over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But as of today, based on our statistics, it appears to be less fatal, because fatality rate for SARS was 10% whereas the coronavirus is 2% to 3%.

sections.label: Bringing symptomatic Singaporeans back
sections.summary: The speaker asks what medical help four Singaporeans with symptoms would receive in Wuhan and whether they could have been brought back for treatment here.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But also sad to hear that the four of them who had symptoms could not be brought back.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I was just wondering what kind of medical help would they receive in Wuhan, if we leave them there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Could we have brought the four of them back as well, in the first place, to receive treatment over here, even if there are symptoms, if their symptoms are not that severe?

sections.label: Wheelchair volunteer and Singaporeans in Wuhan
sections.summary: A wheelchair user offered to man the mask distribution counter, and the speaker wants Singaporeans in Wuhan and Hubei brought back, noting China is responsible and responsive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: He came in a wheelchair and he said that "I can't walk but I can man the counter; can you let me man the mask distribution point?" I would say that this is an opportunity really for all Singaporeans to come together to rally.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We also want to bring all our Singaporeans who are abroad now, who are now in Wuhan, Hubei, if they can come back, please bring them back.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: First of all, let me say that China has been very responsible and very responsive, and is taking all necessary measures to look after our Singaporeans who are still there.

sections.label: Fever and aircraft evacuation decision
sections.summary: The speaker says it was medically unwise to put potentially virus-shedding people on a commercial aircraft, so Chinese authorities rightly decided they should not fly, and remaining Singaporeans will get necessary treatment in China.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The third point I want to make is with respect to the Member's specific query about whether those with fever should have been on board the aircraft.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I think, first of all, if we look – the Member is a doctor – and we all know from a medical point of view, in the context of an epidemic and, particularly, when you are dealing with a global or a potentially global epidemic, it is most unwise to put people on a commercial aircraft when they are potentially actively shedding virus.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, there was good medical rationale and that is why the Chinese authorities make, in my opinion, the right decision that these persons should not fly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I was monitoring the operation and I knew exactly how many were caught in that situation, quite apart from the others who could not evacuate for family reasons because, at that point in time, the decision was that their own citizens were locked down and Singaporeans, PRs and others were considered local citizens.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But, specifically, now for the remaining Singaporeans because we will remain in touch with them, we will do our best to ensure that they have all the necessary treatment in Wuhan or in other places in China.

sections.label: Cooperating with Chinese authorities
sections.summary: The speaker commits to continue working closely with Chinese authorities and says helping them helps everyone collectively.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: That is why we must all cooperate and collaborate to resolve this problem together.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I commit that we will continue to work closely with the Chinese authorities and in any way in which we can help them, it is also helping all of us collectively.
